text: A pre-performance routine (PPR) is any cognitive and behavioral preparation strategy systematically used by an athlete prior to skill execution [ 12 ] PPR interventions typically include various elements that help the athlete adjust arousal levels when necessary (e.g., deep breathing), exert attentional control (e.g., focusing on task-relevant cues or using a “cue word” for concentration), and use behavioral steps relevant to the sport (e.g., bouncing a ball several times before a tennis serve). Psychological advantages of using a PPR may among other things constitute of lowered anxiety [ 13 ], increased task-relevant focus [ 12 ; 14 ], and reduced negative introspection [ 15 ]. Applied sport psychologists suggest that a PPR may be especially used in a closed, self-paced task since there is sufficient time for preparatory strategies before skill execution (e.g., [ 16 , 17 ]).
source_label: Investigating cumulative effects of pre-performance routine interventions in beach volleyball serving
